title: Salamis and Aegina
summary_en: Two islands a short ferry ride from Piraeus with an outsized place in Greek history. Salamis gave its name to the sea battle of 480 BC that saved Athens; Aegina minted some of the first coins in Europe and was the first seat of government of modern Greece. Today one is almost a suburb of Athens, the other an island of pistachio orchards and weekend houses.

sections.en: Salamis: the island of the battle

paras.el: Η Σαλαμίνα είναι πολύ κοντά στον Πειραιά. Με το πλοίο από το Πέραμα η διαδρομή κρατάει μόνο λίγα λεπτά. Πολλοί κάτοικοι δουλεύουν στην Αθήνα και πηγαινοέρχονται κάθε μέρα. Στο νησί υπάρχει ο μεγαλύτερος ναύσταθμος του Πολεμικού Ναυτικού.
paras.en: Salamis (Σαλαμίνα) lies right across the strait from Perama, west of Piraeus; the ferry crossing to the port of Paloukia takes only a few minutes, and many islanders commute to jobs in Athens every day. With about 37,000 permanent residents in 2021, it is the most populous island of the Saronic Gulf, and in summer, when Athenians open their holiday homes, its population swells many times over. The island is also home to the Salamis Naval Base, the main base and headquarters of the Hellenic Navy, and its north-east coast is lined with shipyards.

paras.el: Το 480 π.Χ., στα στενά ανάμεσα στη Σαλαμίνα και στην Αττική, ο ελληνικός στόλος νίκησε τον στόλο των Περσών. Αρχηγός των Αθηναίων ήταν ο Θεμιστοκλής. Η ναυμαχία της Σαλαμίνας είναι μία από τις πιο γνωστές μάχες της αρχαίας ιστορίας. Σύμφωνα με την παράδοση, την ίδια μέρα γεννήθηκε στο νησί ο τραγικός ποιητής Ευριπίδης.
paras.en: In September 480 BC, in the narrow strait between Salamis and Attica, the allied Greek fleet, with the Athenian ships under Themistocles at its core, defeated the much larger fleet of the Persian king Xerxes. The Athenians had abandoned their city, which the Persians burned, and taken refuge on Salamis; Themistocles lured the Persian ships into the narrows, where their numbers counted against them. Herodotus, our main source, describes Xerxes watching the disaster from a throne on the slopes of Mount Aigaleo. Tradition held that the tragic poet Euripides was born on Salamis on the very day of the battle; the island was also the legendary home of Ajax, who led its twelve ships to Troy.

paras.el: Στην αρχαιότητα η Αίγινα ήταν πλούσια και ισχυρή πόλη, με μεγάλο εμπορικό στόλο. Ήταν μία από τις πρώτες πόλεις της Ευρώπης που έκοψαν νομίσματα. Πάνω στα ασημένια νομίσματά της υπήρχε μια θαλάσσια χελώνα. Η Αίγινα και η Αθήνα ήταν για πολλά χρόνια αντίπαλοι.
paras.en: In the archaic period Aegina was a rich maritime city-state and a rival of Athens. It was among the first places in Europe to strike coins: its silver staters, from the second half of the seventh century or the sixth century BC, bear a sea turtle, and the Aeginetan weight standard (a stater of about 12.2 grams divided into two drachmas) was one of the two main standards of the Greek world. After the Athenians defeated the island in the First Peloponnesian War around 456 BC, the sea turtle on the coins was replaced by a land tortoise, a change often read as a symbol of lost sea power. In 431 BC Athens expelled the Aeginetans altogether.

paras.el: Πάνω σε ένα λόφο, μέσα στα πεύκα, στέκεται ο ναός της Αφαίας, μια θεότητα που λατρευόταν κυρίως στην Αίγινα. Ο ναός χτίστηκε γύρω στο 500 π.Χ. και σώζεται πολύ καλά. Τα γλυπτά από τα αετώματά του βρίσκονται σήμερα στο Μόναχο.
paras.en: On a pine-covered hill in the north-east of the island stands the temple of Aphaia, a goddess worshipped chiefly on Aegina and later identified with Athena. The Doric temple was built around 500 BC and is one of the best preserved of its period. Its pedimental sculptures, showing the Trojan wars, were dug up in 1811 by a group of European travellers, bought by Crown Prince Ludwig of Bavaria and restored in Rome; they are now in the Glyptothek in Munich. With the Parthenon and the temple of Poseidon at Sounion, the temple is said to form an “Attic triangle”, a modern legend rather than an ancient plan.

paras.el: Το 1828 ο Ιωάννης Καποδίστριας, ο πρώτος κυβερνήτης της Ελλάδας, ήρθε στην Αίγινα. Το νησί έγινε για λίγο η έδρα της πρώτης ελληνικής κυβέρνησης. Εκεί κόπηκε το πρώτο νόμισμα του νέου κράτους, ο φοίνικας. Ο Καποδίστριας έχτισε και ένα μεγάλο ορφανοτροφείο για τα παιδιά που είχαν χάσει τους γονείς τους στον πόλεμο.
paras.en: In January 1828 Ioannis Kapodistrias, the first Governor of independent Greece, landed on Aegina, which served as the seat of his government until the move to Nafplio in 1829. Here the new state struck its first coin, the phoenix, named after the mythical bird reborn from its ashes. Kapodistrias also built a large orphanage (1828–29) for children orphaned in the War of Independence; the building later housed schools, the first national library and archaeological museum, and the national printing press. From about 1880 it was a prison, and during the junta of 1967–1974 it held political prisoners, which is why locals still call it Οι Φυλακές, “the Prison”.

paras.el: Σήμερα η Αίγινα έχει περίπου 13.000 κατοίκους. Πολλοί Αθηναίοι έχουν εδώ εξοχικά σπίτια. Οι προσκυνητές έρχονται στο μοναστήρι του Αγίου Νεκταρίου, ένα από τα πιο γνωστά προσκυνήματα της Ελλάδας.
paras.en: Today Aegina has about 13,000 permanent residents (2021). Its closeness to Athens, about 40 minutes by fast boat from Piraeus, has made it a favourite place for Athenian holiday homes, and many of the neoclassical houses of the harbour town date from the nineteenth century. Pilgrims come throughout the year to the monastery of Saint Nektarios (1846–1920), a bishop who founded a convent on the island and was canonised in 1961; it is one of the most visited pilgrimage sites in Greece. The small neighbouring island of Agistri, with about 1,100 residents, belongs to the same regional unit of the Islands of Attica.

paras.el: Αν ρωτήσετε έναν Έλληνα τι ξέρει για την Αίγινα, θα σας πει: «το φιστίκι». Τα φιστίκια ήρθαν στο νησί τον 19ο αιώνα. Το 1896 ένας γιατρός, ο Νικόλαος Πέρογλου, ξεκίνησε τη συστηματική καλλιέργεια. Σιγά σιγά οι φιστικιές πήραν τη θέση των αμπελιών.
paras.en: Ask a Greek what Aegina is known for and the answer is likely to be “pistachios”. The pistachio tree reached the island in the nineteenth century, and in 1896 a physician, Nikolaos Peroglou, began growing it systematically. By the middle of the twentieth century pistachio orchards had displaced most other crops, helped by their profitability and by phylloxera, the insect pest that was destroying the island's vineyards. The dry climate and volcanic soil (an extinct volcano makes up two-thirds of the island) suit the tree well.

paras.el: Το «Φιστίκι Αιγίνης» είναι προϊόν Προστατευόμενης Ονομασίας Προέλευσης από το 1996. Κάθε Σεπτέμβριο το νησί γιορτάζει με το «Fistiki Fest». Στα μαγαζιά του λιμανιού πουλάνε φιστίκια ψημένα, αλατισμένα, σε γλυκά, ακόμα και σε παγωτό.
paras.en: “Fistiki Aeginis” has been a Protected Designation of Origin (PDO) product since 1996, which means that only pistachios grown on the island may be sold under that name. About half of the growers belong to the island's agricultural cooperative, and production is estimated at roughly 2,700 tonnes a year. Every September the island holds a pistachio festival, the Fistiki Fest, and the shops along the harbour sell pistachios roasted, salted, in sweets and pastes and even in ice cream. Greeks use the colour φιστικί (“pistachio green”) as an everyday colour word.

grammar.title: Passive aorist in -θηκε/-στηκε: χτίστηκε, γεννήθηκε, κόπηκε
grammar.el: Για γεγονότα του παρελθόντος χρησιμοποιούμε συχνά τον παθητικό αόριστο: ο ναός χτίστηκε, το νόμισμα κόπηκε.
grammar.en: Many verbs of building, making and being born appear in the **passive aorist**, ending in *-θηκε* or *-στηκε* in the 3rd person singular: *χτίζω → χτίστηκε* (was built), *γεννάω/γεννώ → γεννήθηκε* (was born), *κόβω → κόπηκε* (was struck, of a coin), *ενώνω → ενώθηκε* (was united). The plural ends in *-θηκαν/-στηκαν*: *τα γλυπτά βρέθηκαν* (the sculptures were found).

examples.el: Ο ναός χτίστηκε γύρω στο 500 π.Χ.
examples.en: The temple was built around 500 BC.
The first coin was struck there.

grammar.title: Time expressions: για λίγο, σιγά σιγά, κάθε Σεπτέμβριο
grammar.el: Χρήσιμες εκφράσεις για τον χρόνο: για λίγο (for a short time), σιγά σιγά (gradually), κάθε + αιτιατική (every).
grammar.en: **για λίγο** “for a short while”; **σιγά σιγά** “little by little, gradually” (the doubled adverb is very common); **κάθε** + accusative without article for repeated time: *κάθε μέρα, κάθε Σεπτέμβριο*. For a duration, Greek uses **για** + accusative (*για δύο χρόνια*) or the bare accusative (*έμεινε δύο χρόνια*).
